title: The New Social Contract in the Age of Artificial Intelligence · Why read this book?

narrator.label: Narrator
narrator.description: An articulate adult English narrator with warm authority and a thoughtful, varied cadence.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Imagine an automated order offering comfort, safety and varied experiences, if you hand it governance.

direction.delivery: Open warmly, as if presenting a genuine invitation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This book takes that offer seriously, answering with twenty-one debatable clauses of a new social contract.

direction.delivery: Firm and clear; land on twenty-one clauses.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its fear is not scarcity, but a leadership that controls automated infrastructure and cannot be replaced.

direction.delivery: Lower and more serious; stress cannot be replaced.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Administration may be delegated to automated systems, but collective goals must stay under legitimate control.

direction.delivery: Measured; contrast delegated with must stay.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A right to leave a provider counts only if identity, records and services move too.

direction.delivery: Practical, with a slight emphasis on move too.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An appeal needs reasons, corrected facts, independent review and a real remedy.

direction.delivery: Crisp, giving each requirement its own beat.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Those who set goals, run infrastructure and oversee rights must remain separate powers.

direction.delivery: Confident and even, closing the argument.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Later clauses protect attention, privacy, ecological budgets, reproductive freedom and room for new generations.

direction.delivery: Flowing and open, letting the list breathe.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The final chapters ask who pays, who enforces, and why powerful actors would comply.

direction.delivery: Pointed, with a small pause before comply.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its test is clear: abundance is legitimate when it reduces dependency, not when it makes dependency comfortable.

direction.delivery: Clear and weighted; contrast reduces with comfortable.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Begin with the Introduction, where the book sets out the political offer of an automated order.

direction.delivery: Warm and unhurried, a direct invitation.
